definition: Neurofibromatosis is an inherited disorder, passed in an autosomal dominant pattern, that causes tumor growth and related physical abnormalities. It includes two recognized forms: type 1, which is linked with features such as café-au-lait skin spots, multiple neurofibromas, optic nerve gliomas, and bone lesions, and type 2, which is linked with schwannomas, meningiomas, and gliomas.
